events.continuity_hook: This follows the San Diego schedule change that made the original single bayfront hotel less convenient for the work portion of the expo.
events.interaction_goal: Settle the single-stay versus split-stay plan, adjust hotel reservations if needed, protect the spouse weekend add-on, and identify the final confirmations before cancellation windows tighten.
events.scenario_brief: Erin is at the hotel cancellation cutoff for the San Diego expo and needs to decide whether to convert the existing bayfront stay into a split booking. The reopened downtown block room is available Monday through Thursday, which would make the 7:00 a.m. Wednesday breakfast and Thursday teardown much easier, while the bayfront hotel can be shortened to Friday through Sunday for the spouse weekend. Keeping one bayfront reservation avoids repacking but leaves repeated early rideshares and no usable hot tub until Friday; splitting adds luggage storage, check-in timing, and a possible rate mismatch. The spouse's Friday arrival time, the downtown block cancellation terms, and whether the bayfront balcony request carries over on a shortened stay still need confirmation.

events.continuity_hook: This closes the San Diego lodging adjustment after Erin chose the split stay to make the work mornings easier while preserving the weekend hotel.
events.interaction_goal: Run the final San Diego logistics pass for airport timing, hotel changes, luggage storage, rideshares, spouse arrival, expo schedule buffers, seat checks, and weekend transition details.
events.scenario_brief: Five days before leaving for San Diego, Erin has switched to the downtown hotel for Monday through Thursday and the bayfront hotel for Friday through Sunday, with her spouse arriving Friday afternoon on a separate ticket. Her Monday afternoon Denver-to-San Diego nonstop and Sunday afternoon return remain booked, and the downtown hotel confirms fitness access and early bag drop but no pool or hot tub. The bayfront hotel confirms the pool and hot tub should reopen Friday afternoon, while the balcony room remains request-only. The conference app now shows the final booth assignment, Wednesday breakfast location, and Thursday teardown window, but Friday luggage transfer, spouse airport pickup timing, and Sunday return seats still need a practical plan.

events.continuity_hook: This begins Erin's next work-travel episode after the mixed work-and-weekend San Diego trip is complete.
events.interaction_goal: Build a ranked Kansas City plan for arrival timing, flight routing, hotel area, rental car, amenity trade-offs, and the schedule questions to confirm before booking.
events.scenario_brief: After the San Diego expo, Erin is asked to plan an early-spring veterinary lab training week in the Kansas City area, with expected sessions in Overland Park, Lenexa, and North Kansas City. A Monday calibration may become in-person, and she will have a demo analyzer case plus workbook cartons, so rental-car space and hotel parking matter more than restaurant access. A Sunday afternoon Denver-to-Kansas City nonstop gives the cleanest setup but adds a hotel night, while a Monday morning routing saves a night but leaves little room if the calibration is confirmed. Hotel candidates include an Overland Park suite property with strong reviews, free parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness access; a Plaza-area business hotel with better dining but paid parking and fewer recovery amenities; and an airport hotel that simplifies arrival but adds driving on clinic days. The clinic order, Monday requirement, return day, and shipped-kit status are still unresolved.

events.continuity_hook: This narrows the Kansas City plan once the Monday calibration and clinic sequence become firm.
events.interaction_goal: Finalize the outbound flight, hotel, rental car, return-day choice, seat requests, room notes, and expense rationale before the reasonable nonstop fares move.
events.scenario_brief: The coordinator confirms an in-person Monday afternoon calibration in Overland Park, Tuesday training in Lenexa, Wednesday work in North Kansas City, and a Thursday workshop currently expected to end around 1:30 p.m. The Sunday afternoon nonstop from Denver now makes more sense than trying to land Monday morning, and a compact SUV is the practical rental choice for the demo case and cartons. The Overland Park suite hotel can hold a quiet king room with a fridge, free parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness room. The open decision is whether to book the Thursday evening return after pack-up or pay for one more night and take a Friday morning nonstop with less pressure.

events.continuity_hook: This is a post-booking Kansas City adjustment after the final workshop timing and weather risk make the original Thursday return less comfortable.
events.interaction_goal: Compare keeping the Thursday return against moving to Friday morning, then update flight, hotel, rental, drive buffers, and shipment notes if the longer plan is chosen.
events.scenario_brief: After Erin books the Sunday-to-Thursday Kansas City plan, the Thursday workshop is moved later and relocated north of the river, with a 3:00 to 5:00 p.m. wrap-up that makes the same-day return tight. The airline also posts a weather waiver for possible Plains wind and snow on Thursday evening, and the Friday morning nonstop is available without a change fee. The Overland Park hotel can extend the same room by one night, and the rental agency can extend the compact SUV without changing vehicle class. One workbook carton is now scheduled to arrive Wednesday rather than Tuesday, so Erin needs to decide whether the calmer Friday return is worth the added night and how to document the change for work expenses.

events.continuity_hook: This closes the Kansas City planning after Erin accepted the extra hotel night and changed to the calmer Friday return.
events.interaction_goal: Run the final logistics pass for airport timing, rental pickup, winter-weather packing, shipment tracking, daily drive buffers, hotel arrival, return seat selection, and Friday checkout.
events.scenario_brief: Three days before departing for Kansas City, Erin has the Sunday afternoon nonstop, the Overland Park suite hotel through Friday checkout, a compact SUV, and the Friday morning return in place. The airline has moved the outbound about 25 minutes later, but arrival still leaves enough time for hotel check-in and Monday calibration prep. The hotel reconfirms the quiet-room request, fridge, free parking, pool, hot tub, and fitness access. The demo analyzer is already at the Lenexa site, one workbook carton is due at the hotel Monday, and Erin will carry a small consumables kit in her checked bag. A freezing-rain forecast could slow Monday and Wednesday drives, and the return aircraft swap has removed her window-seat assignment.
